newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish carpet maker Gumussuyu to float shares.
newsitem.headline: Turkish carpet maker Gumussuyu to float shares.

text.p: Leading Turkish carpet producer Gumussuyu Hali ve Yer Kaplamalari Sanayi ve Ticaret A.S. will offer 800 billion lira ($7.2 million) nominal-valued new shares to the public, consortium leader Korfez Investment said.
The price in the two-day offer starting on January 23 will be fixed at 1,600 lira for each 1,000 lira nominal-valued share.
Korfez Investment said 45 percent of the offer would be reserved for foreign investors and 15 percent for domestic institutional investors and sale agents of Gumussuyu group.

Consortium members are Global Securities, Alfa Securities, Park Securities and six brokerage houses set up by banks -- Garanti Securities, Inter Investment, Iktisat Securities, Dis Investment, Yasar Investment and Ak Securities.
The company will waive the 800 billion lira of pre-emptive rights to be issued when increasing its capital to 4.5 trillion lira from 3.7 trillion currently, to offer them to the public.

Gumussuyu became a holding company in mid-1996 and transferred all of its machinery, facilities and real-estate to the newly formed group firm Gumussuyu Hali ve Yer Kaplamalari as non-cash capital for the continuation of its carpet business.
It started operations in July 1996 and made 442.63 billion lira of net profits in three months to September 30, 1996. Its net sales were 1.78 trillion lira in the same period.
Korfez Investment said financial debts of Gumussuyu Hali Sanayi were not turned over to Gumussuyu Hali ve Yer Kaplamalar.

Gumussuyu Hali Sanayi had made net profits of 165.69 billion lira and net sales of 2.74 trillion lira in the first half of 1996. It exports 24 percent of turnover and is targeting $30 million in sales this year.

According to a survey prepared by the company, Gumussuyu is the leader in the domestic market with a 41 percent share of branded carpet production, 13 percent of overall carpet production and 24 percent of wall-to-wall carpets.

It has an annual weaving capacity of 10 million square metres in wall-to-wall carpets and six million square metres in individual carpets. The latter is expected to rise to 6.9 million square metres when a $9-million investment is completed by mid-1997.
